fiction.notice: EVERY NAME AND FIGURE IN THIS FILE IS INVENTED. No entity, division, or department here is copied from, derived from, or decodable back to any real organization. Any resemblance to a real company is coincidental.
fiction.purpose: A small, deliberately synthetic catalog sized for a live demo (#92) rather than for realism. It replaces docs/reference/organization-hierarchy.json as the running store's seed; that file stays in the repository as the historical record ADR-0012 describes, and this one is what npm run reset and the in-app reset actually load. See docs/adr/0013-the-demo-catalog-is-the-seed.md.

readMeFirst.shapeAndSize: One legal entity, two divisions, five departments - small enough to narrate live, with just enough departments that the picker still narrows a real list rather than offering one option. Requesting and performing departments in the demo's own story sit in different divisions, so cross-department routing is genuine rather than a same-department shortcut.
readMeFirst.attributes: Every attribute ADR-0012 defines appears at least once - affiliation (legal-entity level, so every department inherits it, demonstrating the full three-level chain even with only one legal entity), jurisdiction (foreign/domestic, on every department), home-office-disclosure (held at the division level on Avionics, so both its departments inherit it and neither carries it directly - the same inheritance case ADR-0012 calls out), offshore-shared-service, and contracting-exception - so the department picker has something real to narrow on (BDR-0008).
readMeFirst.mechanism: Read by the same Fixture schema and transform() that seeded the old 58-department fixture (src/hierarchy/fixture.ts, src/hierarchy/transform.ts). Nothing about the seeding mechanism changed for this catalog; it simply doesn't need the old fixture's chart-specific irregularities (a conflated code column, comma-separated codes, a shared cost centre) because it was authored fresh rather than transcribed from a chart.
